entries.research_question: RQ1 controlled detection; RQ2 closure baselines
entries.claim: In five controlled catalog scenarios SAT-SA emitted every declared finding family (recall 1.0, precision 0.417, F1 0.588; action alignment 4/5). On 12 construction-labelled closures its fast-closure detector tied fixed-threshold and MAD baselines (F1 1.0).
entries.baseline: declared catalog labels; z-score, MAD, IQR, fixed-threshold, seeded random

entries.claim: Hosted validation matched its declared contract in 245/245 perturbed conditions; records shifted outside the assessment period and contradictory records were accepted without warning or output change.
entries.metric: contract match; finding-family change; withheld findings
limitations: not a rate estimate for real data

entries.claim: On one machine with SQLite, LangGraph orchestration produced outputs identical to direct execution and added a median 0.096 s per workflow (95% bootstrap interval -0.020 to 0.211 s, 30 paired runs) and 38 database calls; supervisory finalization took a median 0.288 s.
entries.metric: paired median difference; database calls; stage times

entries.claim: All 36 injected interruptions (6 points x 2 modes x 3 trials) recovered with outputs identical to uninterrupted runs and no completed stage repeated.
TRUST-SAT detected all 13 tested single-field mutations of canonical state in one controlled workflow; a change to an unsigned operational field did not affect verification.

In 96 engineered cohorts the peer rule never fired below 3 peers; with a tight peer spread it flagged every non-median subject from 3 peers, with a wide spread only extreme subjects, fast subjects only from 5 peers.
entries.metric: finding emitted; deviation in MAD units

entries.claim: Removing the fast-closure or negative-space worker lowered catalog micro recall from 1.0 to 0.6; in 5 generated populations (exploratory) four workers lowered ranking quality when present.

Across 20 generated populations SAT-SA ranked generator-labelled pathological entities above random order and alert-volume ranking in 18-20/20 populations per metric; against a closure-speed heuristic recall@20% was higher in 8, equal in 11 and lower in 1.
entries.baseline: random order; critical/high alert volume; fastest median closure

entries.claim: The unchanged pipeline ingested all 134,888 mapped rows (0 rejected) of a real IT incident log (50 groups, 22,604 incidents) and completed analysis for all groups; SAT-SA entity risk was not associated with the groups' SLA-miss rate (Spearman rho -0.11, 95% bootstrap -0.42 to 0.21), while slowest median resolution was (rho 0.94).
entries.baseline: random; incident volume; slowest median resolution; reassignment rate
entries.metric: ingestion counts; Spearman rho; top-quartile P/R/NDCG
limitations: SLA miss measures timeliness, not supervisory quality

entries.research_question: EXT-4 why the external result differed
entries.claim: On the external data, groups with more fast closures missed SLA less (rho -0.70, 95% bootstrap -0.82 to -0.52), so SAT-SA's execution-gap dimension ran opposite to the outcome (rho -0.41); four existence-rule detectors fired for all 50 groups although their input prevalence varied widely; three risk dimensions were unavailable.
entries.metric: Spearman rho; flagging rate; risk dimension spread

entries.claim: HTTP workflow across separate local API and worker processes (SQLite, local storage): 18/18 checks passed; supporting file in the freeze, not a bundle.
limitations: local processes only; containers, PostgreSQL, S3 not exercised
entries.note: recorded as NOT DEMONSTRATED for production-like deployment; the local-process result is in freeze-v2/supporting
